outages.cause: Rolling and emergency blackouts after Russian attacks on energy infrastructure
outages.affected: Ukrenergo said that on Sunday, Nov 15, hourly rolling blackouts of 1 to 2 queues for all consumers, plus industrial capacity limits, are in effect around the clock in parts of Ukraine, eased from Saturday's 1.5 to 3 queues. UNN, citing Ukrenergo, previously said one queue is four hours; the Sunday notice did not restate queue length. No later official Ukrenergo Sunday schedule change was found. Local news outlets, citing DTEK Odeski Elektromerezhi, said the company updated Sunday evening outage schedules for Odesa and the region, with several of 12 queues scheduled off for periods of 1 to 6.5 hours this evening. Overnight outages: DTEK Odeski Elektromerezhi said in a Nov 15 statement that a Russian attack overnight on one of its energy facilities left 41,000 customers without power (no restoration time given; DTEK said crews began work once it was safe, that they were clearing rubble and repairing damaged equipment, that restoration will take time, and that air-raid alerts were significantly complicating the work). Oleh Kiper, head of the Odesa Regional Military Administration, also said around 41,000 customers were temporarily left without electricity after a strike on a DTEK Odesa Electricity Networks facility; Ukraine's State Emergency Service said Russia attacked Chornomorsk, and reporting on the same overnight attack said the city was left without power. No later official customer count or restoration notice was found. Prior Saturday outages with no later official restoration notice found: DTEK Odeski Elektromerezhi said a Russian attack on one of its facilities in the north of Odesa region on the morning of Nov 14 left almost 50,000 customers without power (no restoration time given; DTEK said the facility had been hit repeatedly and that air-raid alerts were complicating the work). As of 5:30 p.m. EET Saturday, Sumyoblenergo said emergency restoration was still underway in part of Sumy region after a large-scale morning outage, and that repeated outages were possible during the work (no customer count released for security reasons). DTEK said Saturday morning that emergency cuts were in effect in the Bucha, Fastiv, and Obukhiv districts of Kyiv region, with stabilization schedules in Kyiv city and the rest of the region. Poltava regional authorities said Saturday that bad weather left about 2,000 subscribers in 13 settlements without power. On Friday, Nov 13, Chernihivoblenergo said an attack left about 150,000 customers without power in the Nizhyn and Pryluky districts; no later Chernihiv customer figure or confirmed restoration was found.
outages.updated: Nov 15, 2026, DTEK Odeski Elektromerezhi official 41,000-customer statement (dated Nov 15); Ukrenergo Sunday schedule per Ukrinform 8:29 p.m. EET Saturday (= 12:29 p.m. CT Saturday); DTEK Odesa evening schedules as reported by Mistogram 5:22 p.m. EET Sunday (= 9:22 a.m. CT) and Odessa-Life 6:20 p.m. EET Sunday (= 10:20 a.m. CT); rechecked 11:51 AM CT Sunday, no later official Ukrenergo schedule change or official restoration figures found for the Odesa or Chernihiv attack outages

outages.cause: Russian attack on a DTEK energy facility
outages.affected: Almost 50,000 customers without power, according to DTEK Odeski Elektromerezhi. Crews began work once it was safe, clearing rubble and repairing damaged equipment; DTEK said the facility had been hit repeatedly, that air-raid alerts were significantly complicating the work, and that restoration will take time. No restoration time was given. This is a separate Nov 14 attack from the overnight Nov 15 DTEK attack that left 41,000 households without power in the Odesa region. No later official customer count or restoration notice was found for this Nov 14 outage.

outages.cause: Russian attack on a DTEK energy facility
outages.affected: 41,000 customers without power, according to a Nov 15 statement by DTEK Odeski Elektromerezhi. DTEK said a Russian attack overnight on Nov 15 hit one of its energy facilities, that 41,000 customers were left without electricity, that crews began work once it was safe, that specialists were inspecting surviving equipment, clearing rubble, and making repairs, that restoration will take a long time, and that air-raid alerts were significantly complicating the work. No restoration time was given. Oleh Kiper, head of the Odesa Regional Military Administration, said around 41,000 customers were temporarily left without electricity after a strike on a DTEK Odesa Electricity Networks facility. Ukraine's State Emergency Service said Russia attacked Chornomorsk; reporting on the same overnight attack said the city was left without power and that six people were injured. No later official customer count or restoration notice was found.

outages.cause: Generation capacity deficit, with several thermoelectric units offline due to breakdowns (Santa Cruz unit 1, Antonio Guiteras, Felton unit 2, and Renté unit 3) and maintenance (Santa Cruz unit 3, Nuevitas unit 5, Felton unit 1, and Renté unit 5); thermal generation is also limited by 251 MW
outages.affected: UNE's Sunday bulletin, published by Cubadebate and attributed to UNE-MINEM, forecast 1,860 MW affected at the evening peak: 970 MW available versus 2,800 MW demand (1,830 MW deficit), if the forecast conditions hold. At 6:00 a.m. Sunday, the grid had 925 MW available versus 2,265 MW of demand, leaving 1,340 MW unserved, and UNE estimated 1,500 MW affected at midday. UNE said Renté unit 3 was expected to add 45 MW at the Sunday evening peak. On Saturday, service was affected by a generation-capacity deficit for all 24 hours and remained affected through the early morning; the maximum Saturday affectation was 1,878 MW at 7:00 p.m. Saturday solar photovoltaic output was 3,116 MWh, with a maximum of 485 MW at midday. No official Sunday midday or evening-peak actual was found. On Sunday, Empresa Eléctrica de La Habana reported generation-deficit outages of 236 MW on 101 distribution circuits at 6:00 a.m. Cuba time, and 220 MW on 105 circuits at 9:15 a.m. Cuba time, according to compilations by CiberCuba and El Alambique. The national grid was not reported as collapsed.
outages.updated: Nov 15, 2026, UNE Sunday bulletin via Cubadebate (attributed to UNE-MINEM); Empresa Eléctrica de La Habana 6:00 a.m. Cuba time Sunday (= 5:00 a.m. CT) as compiled by CiberCuba, and 9:15 a.m. Cuba time Sunday (= 8:15 a.m. CT) as compiled by El Alambique (article timestamped 12:07 p.m.); rechecked 11:51 AM CT, no official Sunday midday or evening-peak actual found

outages.cause: National generation shortfall during evening peak; Tarbela hydropower about 800 MW below normal after reduced water releases following the fifth-extension incident, plus seasonal hydrology and LNG limits
outages.affected: About 1,500 MW national shortfall during evening peak on Nov 11 (peak demand about 16,000 MW vs. about 14,500 MW available), according to ISMO figures cited Nov 12. ISMO said the Nov 10 shortfall, which reached about 2,530 MW, had eased and that generation was back to the routine plan as of Nov 11, but the 1,500 MW evening-peak gap (5 p.m. to 11 p.m.) remained. Discos were following existing 1.5 to 2 hour load-management schedules; The Nation reported some areas still facing up to five hours of additional load-shedding. No later official national ISMO update was found. On Saturday, Nov 14, HESCO spokesman Sadiq Kubar said the Hyderabad utility was receiving 565 MW from the national grid against demand of 1,034 MW, a shortfall of up to 469 MW, and was carrying out an additional 2 hours of load shedding across many feeders until required supply resumed. No customer count was given.
outages.updated: Nov 12, 2026 (ISMO / The Nation); HESCO Saturday statement (UrduPoint / APP, published 9:35 p.m. PKT = 10:35 a.m. CT Saturday); rechecked 11:51 AM CT Sunday, Nov 15, no later official national ISMO update found

outages.place: Mayfair, Crosby, Homestead Park, and nearby Johannesburg suburbs
outages.cause: Fire and a later explosion at the Mayfair substation; after a Thursday-night restoration, the Hursthill substation tripped early Friday because of a network overload. City Power later said the first explosion was caused by cable theft. A separate Crown Substation fault and a Florida Glen cable theft also interrupted supply. On Sunday, City Power said a 16-hour emergency shutdown was needed to complete critical Mayfair Substation repairs
outages.affected: No official customer count. In a Sunday, Nov 15, Mayfair Substation customer alert posted at 12:15 p.m. SAST, City Power said it would implement a 16-hour emergency shutdown from 12:00 noon Sunday to complete critical repairs at the Mayfair Substation and stabilise the network after the prolonged outage. The shutdown would affect customers restored during Phase 1, including the SABC, Netcare Garden City Hospital, and residential customers in Mayfair West. City Power also said Sentech would remain without electricity until multiple cable faults had been located and repaired. SABC News, in a 1:48 p.m. SAST Sunday report, quoted City Power spokesperson Isaac Mangena giving the same shutdown details. No later official notice confirming the shutdown had ended, or giving a new customer count, was found. At 4:24 p.m. SAST Sunday, City Power said power had been fully restored at Florida Glen Substation, after a 33 kV cable was cut and stolen early Saturday; the outage had affected customers in Florida Glen, Quellerina, Industria North, Bergbron, and Northcliff Ext 19. At 7:09 p.m. SAST Sunday, City Power said that because of unforeseen challenges, the Roosevelt Substation cable-fault outage affecting parts of Emmarentia (along Barry, Hertzog, and Muirfield) and Greenside, reported Nov 13, would be attended to in the morning; earlier Sunday it had said the fault had been located and that jointing and termination would commence, and that power in those areas had been partially restored. In a 3:50 p.m. SAST Sunday Hursthill SDC bulletin, City Power said the centre was managing 1,418 open calls, 1,284 of them more than 24 hours old (a wider Hursthill service-area figure, not a customer count for the Mayfair outage alone). That bulletin also said power had been partially restored in Longdale after a Nov 12 Industria Substation cable fault, with two load centres remaining off until repairs were done and the team to return to locate the fault, and that City Power was sourcing a transformer for an Industria Substation outage affecting customers on Kudu Street, reported Nov 13. At 7:37 p.m. SAST Sunday, City Power said a team was on site investigating an unplanned Alexandra Substation outage affecting customers in Riverpark, East Bank, and Tsutsumani; no customer count or restoration time was given. For Florida Substation, City Power said at 12:10 p.m. SAST Sunday that power had been restored except for 3 load centres affected by a burnt mini-substation and attempted vandalism, with the team sourcing materials for repairs, and that the remaining outage affected customers in Florida Lake; no customer count or restoration time was given for those load centres, and no later official update was found. Earlier Saturday, City Power had restored electricity to the SABC, Netcare Garden City Hospital, and residential customers in Mayfair West after overnight repairs and testing at the Hursthill and Mayfair substations, and said engineers would continue preparing for Phase 2, expected to restore remaining affected customers if there were no further technical challenges. No official Phase 2 completion notice was found. In a Saturday afternoon SABC report, City Power's Noel Maso said parts of Mayfair, Auckland Park, Crown Mines, and Vrededorp remained without power, that restoration and replacement costs stood at R24.8 million, and that in a worst-case scenario it could take up to 14 days to restore power to all affected areas. Maso also said a fault at Crown Substation was interrupting supply to Mayfair, Crown Mines, Amalgam, and surrounding communities, and that the Sentech Tower in Brixton was affected, with normal supply then set to be restored by Sunday; no later official confirmation that the Crown Substation fault had been cleared was found. On Sunday afternoon, City Power said power had been restored in Victory Park (Parkhurst Substation; faulty cable reported Nov 14).
outages.etr: City Power said a 16-hour emergency shutdown at Mayfair Substation would run from 12:00 noon Sunday, Nov 15 (SAST), affecting Phase 1 customers including Mayfair West, the SABC, and Netcare Garden City Hospital; no later official notice that the shutdown had ended was found. It gave no separate restoration time for remaining unrestored Mayfair-area customers or for Sentech, which it said would stay off until multiple cable faults were located and repaired. For the Roosevelt Substation outage in parts of Emmarentia and Greenside, City Power said Sunday evening that the outage would be attended to in the morning. For the three remaining Florida Substation load centres in Florida Lake, no restoration time was given. The Florida Glen cable-theft outage was fully restored at 4:24 p.m. SAST Sunday

outages.cause: Drone attacks on power stations and other electricity infrastructure during the war between the Rapid Support Forces and the Sudanese Armed Forces
outages.affected: No official customer count. Al Jazeera, in a Nov 15 report, said the RSF has intensified attacks on power stations around Khartoum state over the past month, creating an energy crisis in the capital, and that there is no clear schedule for the resulting power cuts, which can last anywhere between six hours and a day. It said that between Oct 20 and Nov 2, 2026, there were at least 18 attacks on electricity infrastructure across at least nine states, leading to declining power generation capacity and fuel shortages. Citing The Associated Press, it said repeated drone attacks on power stations have seen electricity generation fall from about 4,400 megawatts before the war to about 1,100 MW today. Residents and a small-business owner in Port Sudan described prolonged, unreliable cuts, including outages lasting more than 24 hours. The UN resident and humanitarian coordinator, Denise Brown, was quoted warning that repeated strikes on power and fuel stations were disrupting dialysis, hospital births, and operations. No later official national customer count or restoration timetable was found.
outages.updated: Nov 15, 2026 (Al Jazeera feature, published Nov 15); generation figure attributed to The Associated Press; rechecked 11:51 AM CT
